messages.subject: prediction for model without latent variables
parts:
Hi,
my model fits well (in theory and model indices, chi-sq, etc) but doesn't use latent variables at all.
This is because I use only one indicator for each model entity.
My data simply doesn't have more possibilities without causing multicollinearity.

However when trying to predict with another dataset with lavPredict( ... type="yhat"/"ov", newdata=newdataset),
I only get predictions for my indepentend variables and not for all, which I would need.
(I don't fully get why this is the case, I guess it is due to some theory of computing predictions)

(I can't just use the same model with latent variables with single indicators, because I'm getting
negative (residual) variances as result of a rather small data set and very skew distributions)

Cheers
Lukas

parts: my model doesn't use latent variables at all... when trying to predict with another dataset with lavPredict( ... type="yhat"/"ov", newdata=newdataset), I only get predictions for my indepentend variables and not for all, which I would need.
(I don't fully get why this is the case, I guess it is due to some theory of computing predictions)

In lavaan, the predict() method is written for computing factor scores, not predicted values of observed variables.  This is because in covariance structure analysis, the "data" analyzed/explained/predicted is the covariance matrix and mean vector, not the N x P data table of cases by variables.  This is why the fitted() method returns the model-implied covariance matrix and mean vector in lavaan, whereas for the (g)lm function, it is redundant with the predict() method when no new data are passed for prediction.

What do you need the predicted values for?  If it is only a path analysis, then you can just fit a univariate multiple-regression model to each outcome with the (g)lm function, and pass your new data using the predict() methods for those objects.  

Alternatively, Jarrett Byrnes wrote some code to provide predicted values of outcome variables from lavaan objects, which I hope to eventually incorporate into the semTools package (unless Yves plans to incorporate it into lavaan).  You can grab his code here and use it; hopefully it works.

https://github.com/jebyrnes/semTools/blob/master/semTools/R/fitted_lavaan.R

used lavaan sem() function to fit the model
